subject: DPA follow-up: custody & provenance for ingest handoff
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alexr@medicor.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medicor Legal <legal@medicor.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T10:15:00-04:00
Subject: Re: DPA and dataflow clarifications - ingest handoff

Hi Hannah / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare procurement, our legal team has two specific asks we need you to confirm before we can sign the DPA: (1) a short, firm commitment on custody (who holds the encryption keys for inbound patient data during the ingest process) and (2) an annotated data-flow diagram that shows the handoff point between our connector and Redwood's proxy/ingest (we need to show this to auditors).

We attached a short redline of your standard DPA and highlighted the sections where we need explicit custody language and audit log retention (see attachment: redlines_medico_dpa_20260902.pdf). Also — are there subprocessors involved in the ingestion pipeline (we specifically need any third-party transform or tokenization vendors listed)?

Can you get us the diagram and a one-paragraph answer on key custody and KMS terms by EOD Friday? If not, propose an alternate timeline.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Senior Security Program Manager
Medicor Health
(attachment: redlines_medico_dpa_20260902.pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alexr@medicor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA and dataflow clarifications - ingest handoff

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. We're happy to tighten the language and provide the diagram. Quick answers up front:
- Custody: Redwood does not hold customer master keys by default. For Medicor we propose KMS key custody options in the DPA (customer-managed KMS with an option for Redwood to hold an envelope key if required for managed key workflows).
- Audit logs: we can commit to a 12-month log retention for ingest/audit traces with export on request; if you need longer we can evaluate as an add-on in procurement.
- Subprocessors: there are two potential subprocessors in the ingest path (third-party connector hosting and a managed-tokenization service). I'll attach an annotated roster and a draft dataflow diagram.

Marissa — can you attach the data-flow image and the current subprocessor roster and suggested DPA clause text for custody/KMS? Kimberly, please flag any security caveats on retention or exportability.

I'll propose a 30-minute hangout Friday 09/04 14:00 ET to walk through the diagram with your team. If that works for you Alex, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Sales, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(attachment: ingest-handoff-dataflow-v1.png)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA and dataflow clarifications - ingest handoff

Adding the artifacts per Hannah's request. Notes below:

- Attached: subprocessor_roster_20260831.csv (rows: connector-hosting-provider, tokenization-svc, telemetry-aggregation). We call out the tokenization service as a subprocessor that only receives pseudonymized payloads; original PHI remains encrypted in transit and at rest.
- Dataflow diagram (ingest-handoff-dataflow-v1.png): shows the connector (Medicor) -> TLS to Redwood ingress -> transient staging on dedicated GPU pool (encrypted) -> tokenization (third-party) -> model runtime. The diagram annotates custody boundaries and where envelope keys are used.
- Draft DPA clause (suggestion): "Customer retains key ownership. Redwood may hold an envelope key strictly for managed-decryption operations; envelope key usage is auditable and reversible. Redwood will provide KMS attestation documentation on request."

Security notes from my review:
- We should avoid a blanket 24/7 data access guarantee; instead offer operational playbook and SOC2 evidence.
- For audit log export, we'll provide monthly exports by default and ad-hoc exports within 5 business days when requested by customer legal.

I'll attach the two files here for sending to Medicor.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20260831.csv, ingest-handoff-dataflow-v1.png

-Marissa
Sr. Privacy Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alexr@medicor.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medicor Legal <legal@medicor.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: DPA and dataflow clarifications - ingest handoff

Hannah / Marissa — thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed the artifacts; a few redline points below (we've attached updated redline PDF):
1) KMS custody: Medicor's legal insists on a clause that explicitly states Redwood will not have access to unencrypted PII without a documented, auditable request flow and customer authorization. Your draft looks good but can you commit to the flow being enforced by X-ray logs (or equivalent) and provide sample log schema?
2) Subprocessors: we need a commitment to notify within 30 days of any new subprocessor that will process ingest payloads and an option for Medicor to request a pipeline-only onshore hosting carve-out.
3) Dataflow: the diagram is helpful; can the annotated PNG include a numbered legend that maps each hop to the DPA section/relevant evidence artifact (SOC2 page, KMS attestation, subprocessor contract id)? That's what our auditors will want.

We can do the 09/04 14:00 ET call — please send invite. Our legal will join to walk the redlines.

Best,
Alex
(attachment: redlines_medico_dpa_20260903.pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alexr@medicor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-05T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA and dataflow clarifications - ingest handoff

Alex — good points. Plan and owners: 
- KMS custody/log schema: Kimberly will produce a sample log schema and a short attestation package by Thursday 09/10. It will show the request flow, envelope-key usage, and the fields auditors typically request. (Owner: kimberly_park)
- Subprocessor notice: we can add a 30-day notice obligation for new ingestion-path subprocessors plus the onshore carve-out option (commercial impact to be discussed). I'll get legal to prepare the exact redline. (Owner: hannah_schmitt)
- Diagram/legend: Marissa will update the PNG with a numbered legend mapping hops to evidence artifacts and a pointer to our Drive folder. (Owner: marissa_cole)

I'll send the 09/04 invite in a separate calendar note for the walkthrough. For now, please accept these actions as our commitment to resolve the outstanding redlines prior to final signature. If Medicor needs a binding SLA for key custody beyond the draft DPA language, we can evaluate and include in the SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
Hannah
